facts.fact: Per a 2018 Patrick McMahon analysis cited by the page, campaigns waste 88.5% of every ad buy in Arizona's 1st Congressional District on viewers who can't vote for them.
facts.quote: campaigns waste 88.5% of every ad buy reaching viewers who can't vote for them

facts.fact: Per a 2018 Ad Age article cited by the page, 79.1% of political TV spend in Northern Kentucky goes to households in Ohio and Indiana.
facts.quote: In Northern Kentucky, 79.1% of political TV spend goes to households in Ohio and Indiana

facts.fact: The page states that DMA-based buying has cost campaigns over $80 million in wasted impressions broadcasting to voters outside their districts; no specific source is attributed for this figure.
facts.quote: DMA-based buying has cost campaigns over $80 million in wasted impressions broadcasting to voters outside their districts

facts.fact: Per FreeWheel via BusinessWire (2025), CTV political ad spending is projected to reach $2.5 billion for the 2026 midterms, a 128% increase over 2022.
facts.quote: CTV political ad spending is projected to hit $2.5 billion for the 2026 midterms, a 128% increase over 2022

facts.fact: The page states there are 210 Designated Market Areas (DMAs) in the United States.
facts.quote: There are 210 DMAs in the United States, and they were designed for commercial advertising, not politics.

facts.fact: Per Crain's Chicago Business (2018), 47% of political TV and radio ad spending in the St. Louis market from January 2017 through Election Day 2018 went to cross-border candidates reaching voters in the other state.
facts.quote: 47% of political TV and radio ad spending in the St. Louis market went to Illinois candidates reaching Missouri voters

facts.fact: The page gives an illustrative example in which a race covering 100,000 households inside a DMA of 2 million households would have 95% waste.
facts.quote: For a race covering 100,000 households inside a DMA of 2 million, that's 95% waste.

facts.fact: The page recommends allocating 20-30% of total budget to the early campaign phase (6+ months out), focused on name recognition in high-population areas.
facts.quote: Budget allocation: 20-30% of total.

facts.fact: The page recommends allocating 15-25% of total budget to the primary season phase.
facts.quote: Budget allocation: 15-25%.

facts.fact: The page recommends allocating 45-60% of total budget to the general election push in the final 8 weeks.
facts.quote: Budget allocation: 45-60%.

facts.fact: The page names L2 and Data Trust as providers of party affiliation and voter history data that can be layered onto CTV geotargeting.
facts.quote: Party affiliation and voter history** from providers like L2 and Data Trust

facts.fact: Typical CPMs for political advertising on CTV range from $25 to $40, depending on targeting precision and inventory demand.
facts.quote: Typical CPMs for [political advertising](https://adwave.com/resources/political-ad-rates-2026) on CTV range from $25 to $40, depending on targeting precision and inventory demand.

facts.fact: The page states that a broadcast buy in a major DMA might cost $50,000 per week while reaching only a fraction of a campaign's actual voters.
facts.quote: a broadcast buy in a major DMA might cost $50,000 per week to reach a fraction of your actual voters.

facts.fact: The page states that a geotargeted CTV campaign reaching only a district's households might cost $2,000 to $5,000 per week for comparable voter impressions.
facts.quote: A geotargeted CTV campaign reaching only your district's households might cost $2,000 to $5,000 per week for comparable voter impressions, with zero waste.

facts.fact: Adwave says campaigns can start with as little as $30 a day on its platform.
facts.quote: platforms like [Adwave](https://adwave.com/how-it-works/) let you start with as little as $30 a day and target voters in specific ZIP codes across 100+ streaming networks.

facts.fact: Adwave says its platform reaches voters across 100+ streaming networks.
facts.quote: target voters in specific ZIP codes across 100+ streaming networks.

facts.fact: A FAQ on the page says Adwave lets campaigns start with as little as $50, which conflicts with the $30-per-day figure given elsewhere on the page.
facts.quote: Platforms like Adwave let campaigns start with as little as $50, making TV advertising viable for city council, school board, and other

facts.fact: The page says CPM rates for CTV political ads climb during peak season, which it defines as September through Election Day.
facts.quote: During peak political season (September through Election Day), rates climb as inventory tightens.

facts.fact: The page claims ZIP code targeting on CTV eliminates 90%+ of the waste inherent in broadcast buying for most campaigns (vendor claim).
facts.quote: For most campaigns, ZIP code targeting eliminates 90%+ of the waste inherent in broadcast buying.

facts.fact: The page recommends starting geotargeted ads 6+ months before Election Day with broader targeting, then tightening to high-priority precincts in the final 8 weeks.
facts.value: 6+ months before Election Day; final 8 weeks
facts.quote: Most campaigns benefit from starting 6+ months before Election Day with broader geographic targeting for name recognition, then tightening to high-priority precincts in the final 8 weeks.

facts.fact: The page recommends saturating high-priority precincts with turnout-focused messaging in the final 72 hours before an election.
facts.quote: **Final 72 hours:** Saturate high-priority precincts with turnout-focused messaging.
